verdict.detail: The album first came out in 1968 (US).

notes.text: UK stereo reissue in outside-laminated gatefold cover

, on black/silver-print Verve Records labels.
Poly-lined 'Plastic Bags Can Be Dangerous' standard inner sleeve with 'British Patent No. 800513 & 973939' and 'Made In England'. 
First catalogue number on cover, 2nd on labels.

Cover: Censored lyrics. 
Vinyl: Partially censored lyrics.
Technically, this is a different album to the 1st issue

, which had fully censored vinyl content.
UK '2nd censored' issue with group in dresses on outer face. 
The 'Sgt Pepper' pastiche features inside and later became the cover, as was initially intended.

Sleeve printed and made by E. J. Day Group, London & Bedford. See also very similar

where the sleeve is printed by Howard Printers (Slough) Ltd. England.

Label has the original MGM "Made Under Licence From Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc., Owners Of The Trade Mark 'Verve'" text above the silver 'T' motif, plus other minor variations in comparison with later* releases. (*as found on UK Howard Printers sleeved label version)

Track A2 errata: on label has "Need" instead of "Needs".
Track B4 is titled as "It's His Voice On The Radio" on cover, but correctly credited as "Lonely Little Girl" on label.

"This Whole Monstrosity Was Conceived & Executed By Frank Zappa As A Result Of Some Unpleasant Premonitions, August Through October 1967."
"All the music heard on this album was composed, arranged & scientifically mutilated (with the exception of a little bit of surf music). None of the sounds are generated electronically ... they are all the product of electronically altering the sounds of NORMAL instruments."

"The Present Day Composer Refuses To Die!" (Edgard Varese, July 1921)
